documents.title: IPCC Assessment on Lifecycle Emissions of Clean Electricity
documents.summary: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) comprehensive lifecycle analysis across generation sources including construction, mining, and decommissioning.
documents.evidence: Nuclear power produces a median of 12g CO2-equivalent per kWh of electricity—identical to offshore wind and 4x lower than solar PV (48g CO2/kWh), while operating with a 92% capacity factor compared to 25% for solar and 35% for onshore wind.
citations: IPCC Fifth Assessment Report (AR5), Working Group III, Table A.III.2
International Energy Agency (IEA), 'Nuclear Power and Secure Energy Transitions', 2022

documents.title: Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) & Passive Safety Architecture
documents.summary: Engineering review of Generation IV SMRs designed to utilize natural convection and gravity rather than active AC electrical pumps for emergency cooling.
documents.evidence: SMR designs like NuScale and Westinghouse AP300 incorporate passive containment heat removal that can withstand prolonged station blackouts indefinitely without operator intervention or external power, eliminating Fukushima-style loss-of-coolant meltdown hazards.
citations: World Nuclear Association, 'Small Modular Reactor Developments', 2024
US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) Design Certifications

documents.title: Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) & Construction Timelines
documents.summary: Lazard benchmark comparing levelized costs and construction durations between conventional nuclear and utility-scale solar and battery storage.
documents.evidence: Unsubsidized nuclear LCOE ranges from $141 to $221 per MWh, compared to $24–$96 for utility-scale solar and $34–$110 for onshore wind. Landmark projects like Vogtle Units 3 & 4 suffered 7-year construction delays and ballooned from $14 billion to over $35 billion, demonstrating prohibitive financial risk.
citations: Lazard Levelized Cost of Energy Analysis (LCOE 16.0), 2023
MIT Energy Initiative, 'The Future of Nuclear Energy in a Carbon-Constrained World'
